headline: High-risk shared filesystem and shell access make prompt injection, data leakage, and cascading errors plausible; Plane adds no write isolation.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Claude Code reads and writes repo files and uses MCP; Plane can surface files, hyperlinks, notes, and uploads. If Plane content is copied into Claude Code or shared via files, attacker-controlled text can steer tool use. Plane itself is not an instruction parser, so this is interaction-driven rather than default-critical.
conditions: IF Plane content is transferred into Claude Code via shared files or copy-paste, prompt injection becomes plausible.
IF an MCP server exposes Plane content without provenance labels, Claude Code may treat it as instructions.
mitigations: Disable automatic ingestion of Plane exports into Claude Code.
Use a read-only staging folder for any Plane files.
Prefix imported content with a provenance banner.
Review MCP server outputs before passing them to Claude Code.
requires-engineering: add content provenance tagging between systems.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Claude Code has broad network egress and handles git credentials and environment secrets; Plane touches files, notes, and hyperlinks. If the same workspace or files are shared, Claude Code can exfiltrate sensitive repo data while Plane stores or displays it. Plane is not write-capable, but that does not block leakage from Claude Code.
conditions: IF both agents access the same workspace or uploaded files, sensitive content can flow from Plane into Claude Code outputs.
IF Claude Code is allowed to send repository context to external APIs, leakage risk increases.
mitigations: Separate workspaces for the two agents.
Remove secrets from the shared directory before running Claude Code.
Restrict Claude Code network egress during sensitive tasks.
Avoid uploading Plane attachments into the coding workspace.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention controls.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Claude Code can write the filesystem and modify git state; Plane cannot write the filesystem, so direct write-write conflict is limited. However, both can touch shared files through uploads or repo files, and Claude Code runs as the invoking user with no self-isolation. That creates a real but not maximal conflict surface.
conditions: IF Plane uploads are placed in the same directory Claude Code edits, file clobbering can occur.
IF Claude Code modifies git state while another process edits the same repo, conflicts can arise.
mitigations: Use separate directories for uploads and code edits.
Pause one agent before the other writes to the repo.
Commit or stash before switching agents.
Keep Plane attachments read-only in the coding workspace.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared mutable paths.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Claude Code can generate code, patches, and shell actions; Plane can present issues, tasks, and notes that may be treated as authoritative inputs. If Plane output is forwarded into Claude Code without verification, errors can cascade into commits or shell commands. The pair does not prove automation, so medium fits.
conditions: IF Plane issue text is copied into Claude Code as ground truth, downstream mistakes can propagate.
IF Claude Code is instructed to act on Plane tasks without human review, erroneous actions can be committed.
mitigations: Require human review before executing Claude Code suggestions.
Cross-check Plane facts against source artifacts.
Mark Plane-derived text as untrusted input.
Use a checklist before git commits or shell execution.
requires-engineering: add verification gates between task intake and action execution.

E_compliance.rationale: Claude Code handles git credentials and local files on the invoking host, while Plane is a self-hosted issue tracker with file uploads and support channels. The profiles do not show a residency or certification mismatch, so only a small compliance gap is evidenced. The other agent is cited because the risk is about data classes and hosting surfaces in both systems.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into Plane uploads and then mirrored into Claude Code, retention and access controls must be checked.
IF the deployment uses different retention policies for repo files and issue attachments, compliance drift can occur.
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated data in shared files.
Document retention for Plane uploads and repo artifacts.
Review access to git credentials on the host.
Use separate accounts for issue tracking and coding.
requires-engineering: align retention and residency controls across systems.
